jobs.title: Graduate Student Assistant (TUC - College of Business & Economics) at The University Corporation
jobs.description: Employer: The University Corporation Expires: 11/29/2026 About The University Corporation The University Corporation is a non-profit auxiliary corporation providing commercial and administrative services to California State University, Northridge. Our mission is to provide services and solutions that address the needs of California State University, Northridge; to support the academic, research, and creative endeavors of its students, faculty, and staff; and to enhance the quality of campus life. https://www.csun.edu/tuc The Center for Fintech Innovation and Policy at CSUN’s David Nazarian College of Business and Economics is seeking a graduate student assistant to support the Center’s day-to-day operations. The Center is a hub connecting Los Angeles’s fintech industry with CSUN’s students and faculty. Its work spans five areas: student development through mentorship, career days, and a policy fellows program; digital engagement through webinars and podcasts with regulators, scholars, and practitioners; skills-based certifications; applied research and policy on fintech, AI, and financial regulation; and a direct connection between industry and the university.The Center recently received a multi-year, multi-million-dollar grant from the U.S. Department of Education, in partnership with Cal State LA, to build a venture studio in which students learn how financial technology works, build a product with AI tools, and pitch it to industry. Duties and Responsibilities:Working closely with the Director, the student assistant will help run the Center’s daily business. This includes outreach and marketing, managing social media and promotional materials, organizing and scheduling meetings and events, coordinating internal communications and logistics across the team, and reaching out to stakeholders across the university, such as the grants office, faculty, advising offices, student organizations, and campus departments. The assistant will also help with recruitment, support the Center’s research, prepare and proofread documents and correspondence, maintain program records, and take on other tasks as the Center’s needs arise. Qualifications:Applicants must be currently enrolled graduate students in good standing with a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher. We are looking for someone who is organized, detail-oriented, and reliable, with strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to manage several tasks and deadlines at once. Experience withsocial media and social media advertising, event planning, AI tools, and design tools is a plus, as is an interest in fintech, AI, or entrepreneurship. This position offers hands-on experience in program leadership in a new andgrowing center. Pay, Benefits, & Work ScheduleThis position is employed through The University Corporation (TUC).Schedule: Varies Based on Hiring Manager (10 - 20 hours per week)The anticipated hiring range: $20.00 per hourTime Base: Part-Time General InformationIn accordance with the California State University (CSU) Out-of-State Employment Policy, TUC is a state entity whose business operations reside within the State of California and prohibits hiring employees to perform work outside of California. The hiring department will contact the best-qualified candidates and invite them to participate in the interview process.Application Screening begins November 6, 2026 and will continue until the position is filled. To be considered in the initial review, applications must be submitted before the date listed above. Application submissions received after the application screening date will be reviewed at the discretion of the University. For more detailed information on the application and hiring process, please view the link below: http://www-admn.csun.edu/ohrs/employment/ Equal Employment OpportunityThe University Corporation is an Equal Opportunity Employer and prohibits discrimination based on race, color, ethnicity, religion, national origin, age, gender, gender identity/expression, sexual orientation, genetic information, medical condition, marital status, veteran status, and disability. jobs.title: IT Technology Experience and Engagement Student Assistant at CSUN 10052 - Information Technology
jobs.description: Employer: CSUN 10052 - Information Technology Expires: 12/02/2026 Position Overview The Division of Information Technology is seeking a motivated and curious student to help improve the technology experience for CSUN students. This position will serve as a student voice and technology ambassador, helping IT better understand how students experience campus technology, where challenges or pain points exist, and how current services can be improved. The Student Technology Experience & Engagement Assistant will evaluate existing IT services and tools from a student perspective, test digital experiences such as websites and chatbots, gather feedback from other students and student organizations, and communicate findings and recommendations to IT staff and leadership.This role is ideal for a student who enjoys asking questions, solving problems, communicating with others, and thinking creatively about how technology can better support the student experience. Key Responsibilities Student Technology Experience & Service ImprovementIdentify technology-related pain points or challenges students experience while navigating CSUN systems, services, and processes.Select specific student technology experiences to evaluate from beginning to end.Document how a service currently works from the student perspective and identify areas that may be confusing, difficult, inefficient, or unclear.Work with the IT team responsible for the service to better understand the current process and explore opportunities for improvement.Recommend ways to make technology services more intuitive, accessible, and student-friendly. Technology Testing & User ExperienceTest existing and emerging IT services, tools, websites, forms, applications, and digital experiences from a student perspective.Evaluate tools such as IT chatbots and self-service resources to determine whether information is accurate, easy to find, and helpful to students.Participate in testing new features, designs, services, or technology prior to or after implementation.Document testing results, usability issues, and recommendations for improvement.Consider how emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, could improve the student technology experience. Student Outreach & EngagementServe as a liaison between students and the Division of Information Technology.Work with student representatives and organizations to gather feedback about technology experiences and needs.Conduct informal interviews, surveys, focus groups, or other feedback activities with students.Help IT better understand whether students are aware of the technology services and resources currently available to them.Identify opportunities to improve how IT communicates available services to the student body. Student Ambassador RoleRepresent the student perspective in discussions about IT services, technology, and digital experiences.Advocate for solutions that consider usability, accessibility, communication, and the needs of students.Help connect IT teams with appropriate student groups when additional feedback or testing is needed.Act as a champion for improving the student technology experience across campus. Research, Analysis & RecommendationsOrganize and summarize feedback collected from students.Identify common themes, recurring concerns, and opportunities for improvement.Research how students currently discover and use IT services.Help evaluate what a positive technology experience should look like from a student perspective.Develop recommendations based on student feedback, testing, and observations. Presentations & CommunicationPrepare clear summaries, reports, presentations, or visual materials describing findings and recommendations.Present student feedback and technology experience findings to IT staff and leadership.Communicate observations professionally and constructively.Participate in meetings with IT teams, campus partners, and student representatives. Qualifications:RequiredCurrently enrolled CSUN student.Strong verbal and written communication skills.Comfortable speaking with students, staff, and university leadership.Strong curiosity and willingness to ask questions.Ability to look at a process critically and identify potential areas for improvement.Strong attention to detail and organizational skills.Ability to work independently and collaboratively.Willingness to test technology and provide candid, constructive feedback.Interest in improving the student experience.PreferredInterest in technology, user experience, communications, business analysis, design, marketing, research, or related areas.Experience working with student organizations, campus programs, or student leadership.Experience conducting surveys, interviews, focus groups, or collecting feedback.Familiarity with CSUN technology systems and services.Interest in artificial intelligence and emerging technologies.Experience creating or delivering presentations. Hours: Up to 20 hours per week, depending on the student's class schedule and departmental needs. This position is semester-based and eligible for renewal.

jobs.title: Student Success & Belonging Librarian at CSUN 10050 - University Library
jobs.description: Employer: CSUN 10050 - University Library Expires: 11/17/2026 Tenure-Track Faculty Position AnnouncementDepartment: Research, Instruction, & Outreach ServicesRank: Senior Assistant Librarian Effective Date of Appointment: July 1, 2027 (Subject to Budgetary Approval)Anticipated Hiring Range: $85,524 to $99,420 (Dependent upon qualifications) CSUN’s Commitment to You:CSUN is committed to achieving excellence through teaching, scholarship, learning and inclusion. Our values include a respect for all people, building partnerships with the community and the encouragement of innovation, experimentation, and creativity. CSUN strives to cultivate a community in which a diverse population can learn and work in an atmosphere of civility and respect. CSUN is especially interested in candidates who make contributions to equity and inclusion in the pursuit of excellence for all members of the university community. As a Hispanic-serving Institution (HSI), inclusiveness and diversity are integral to CSUN’s commitment to excellence in teaching, research, and engagement. As of Fall 2025, CSUN enrolls 36,960 students, where 57.5% are Latinx, 18.4% are White, 8.5% are Asian-American, 5.5% are Black/African American, 0.1% are Native American, and 0.1% are Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander. For more information about the University, visit: http://www.csun.edu About the College:For more information about the University Library, please visit: http://library.csun.edu About the Department:For more information about the Department of Research, Instruction, & Outreach Services, please visit: https://library.csun.edu/about/contacts-departments/rios Position:In support of its service and information literacy mission, the department of Department of Research, Instruction, & Outreach Services at California State University, Northridge (CSUN) is seeking a tenure-track Student Success & Belonging Librarian at the rank of Senior Assistant Librarian. This position will be an innovative and self-motivated librarian to partner with students to ensure they feel connected, supported, and empowered throughout their academic journey for the Department of English, particularly Approaches to University Writing courses for General Education credit. This librarian collaborates closely with faculty to help students build strong, critical information literacy skills that strengthen their academic confidence and success, through culturally responsive services, campus partnerships such as the Learning Resource Center, and a deep commitment to equity.The successful candidate will provide general and/or discipline-specific library and information literacy instructional services; develop discipline-specific online research guides and/or digital learning objects (DLOs) in support of student research needs; provide reference assistance and research consultations in-person and virtually; conduct outreach to faculty and student organizations; participate in collection development for the Department of English; support faculty research and scholarly communications; and serve on library, campus, regional, and national initiatives or committees. The position requires weekly reference hours, attending faculty meetings, participation in assessment of student learning, and service to the department, college, and university. The successful candidate may be required to teach and provide reference services on weekdays, evenings, weekends, and/or online. Given CSUN’s commitment to excellence in teaching, research, and engagement in a diverse environment, the successful candidate will help the Department achieve equitable academic outcomes for all students through teaching, research support, scholarship, and service. This is a 12-month, full-time, tenure-track faculty position at the Senior Assistant Librarian level, with attendant expectations for professional competence, service, and scholarship. Some evening and weekend work is required. The successful candidate will be held to the standards and requirements of the University Library and Research, Instruction and Outreach Services (RIOS) department in which they are housed for recommending tenure and promotion. Required Qualifications:• Master’s degree in information and/or library science from an ALA-accredited school, or equivalent degree if earned outside the U.S. or Canada• Experience providing reference assistance (e.g. virtual, in-person, and/or research consultations)•Teaching experience providing information literacy library instruction, or as the instructor in writing-intensive courses• Ability to apply culturally responsive pedagogies and instruction practices that lead to equitable outcomes for all students• Effective written communication, interpersonal, organizational, and problem-solving skills• Commitment to engage in research and continued professional development that would lead to promotion and tenure as a faculty member in the California State University system Preferred Qualifications:• Undergraduate or graduate degree in English, Rhetoric, or closely related, writing intensive discipline• Evidence of effective engagement OR potential to engage with a diverse student body• Experience using culturally responsive pedagogy, in person in the classroom, that leads to equitable outcomes for all students• Experience creating a student-centered learning environment• Outreach experience that includes working with students from diverse backgrounds• Experience adopting inclusive approaches to reference Application Deadline:Preferred application deadline is November 16, 2026 and applications received after this date may be considered on an as-needed basis. jobs.title: Research Assistant at CSUN 24200 - Autonomy Research Center for STEAHM
jobs.description: Employer: CSUN 24200 - Autonomy Research Center for STEAHM Expires: 12/02/2026 Research Assistant — Convergence Research, Innovation, and Societal Impact Book ProjectPosition: Undergraduate or Graduate Research AssistantFaculty Lead: Dr. Nhut Tan HoSenior Advisor: Dr. Peter GrayProject: Convergence in Action: How Deep Integration Across Disciplines and Sectors Turns Complex Problems into Innovation and Societal ImpactHours: Approximately 10 hours/week, depending on assignmentCompensation and duration: $18/hour and academic year, with possibility of continuation Project DescriptionStudents are invited to participate in the research and development of a book examining how universities, government, industry, and other organizations work across disciplinary and institutional boundaries to address complex societal and technological problems.The book will draw on case studies from the National Science Foundation's convergence research programs, selected MIT and other universities’ initiatives, and the NASA-sponsored Autonomy Research Center for STEAHM (ARCS) at CSUN. It will investigate not only what these projects accomplished, but how successful convergence efforts are designed and operated.Major questions include:What distinguishes genuine convergence from conventional interdisciplinary research?How are effective cross-disciplinary and cross-sector teams created?How are complex societal problems identified and framed?How do teams integrate different disciplines, methods, and perspectives?How do government, industry, communities, and end users participate?What organizational barriers prevent convergence?How does research move toward innovation and societal impact?What institutional practices make convergence sustainable?Student Responsibilities:Depending on interests and background, research assistants may participate in one or more of the following:research NSF-funded convergence projects and investigators;collect and verify project information from authoritative sources;search scholarly literature, reports, project websites, publications, patents, and other evidence of outcomes;develop structured case-study research dossiers;analyze how multidisciplinary teams were formed and operated;identify evidence of research translation and societal impact;conduct background research on interview subjects;assist in preparing interview questions;organize and analyze interview transcripts;code interviews and cases for recurring themes and lessons learned;maintain bibliographic records and research databases;research MIT and other institutional convergence models;document lessons from ARCS projects and participants;prepare concise research summaries, tables, timelines, and visual materials;support fact-checking, references, and manuscript development.Students will not simply summarize sources. They will be trained to analyze each case using a common framework:Problem → Team → Integration → Stakeholders → Translation → Outcomes → LessonsDesired QualificationsStrong candidates will have:intellectual curiosity and interest in research, innovation, technology, or societal problems;strong reading and analytical skills;careful attention to evidence and accuracy;ability to summarize complex material clearly;reliability and ability to work independently;strong written English;comfort learning topics outside their primary discipline.Students from all disciplines are encouraged to apply, including engineering, computer science, social sciences, humanities, business, health sciences, communication, design, and education.Prior research experience is helpful but not required.Particularly Valuable SkillsExperience with any of the following is useful:literature searches;qualitative research;interview analysis;data organization;Zotero or other reference-management software;Excel/Google Sheets;bibliographic databases;visualization;AI-assisted research tools used responsibly;technical or science writing.What Students Will LearnStudents will gain experience in:convergence and interdisciplinary research;science and innovation policy;qualitative and case-study research;scholarly literature review;analysis of large research programs;interviewing and qualitative coding;research translation and societal-impact assessment;working directly with faculty and national research leaders.Students may also have opportunities to participate in conversations with researchers, government program leaders, university leaders, and other experts involved in major convergence initiatives.ApplicationInterested students should submit their application package below to this link https://forms.gle/6GaGcmpLwyqb28F48 :a brief statement of interest (approximately 250 words);résumé/CV;academic major and year;description of any relevant research, writing, data, or analytical experience;one example of a complex problem or project that interests you and why you think multiple disciplines would be needed to address it.
